content: Bone Three blueprint received: Four integration paths for wiring local 3B LoRA compass model as preprocessing router inside Claude ecosystem. Path A (FastMCP MCP server, ~50 lines Python) works across Cowork and Claude Code. Path B (UserPromptSubmit hook) gives deterministic classification in Claude Code only. Recommended: layer both. Key insight: MCP servers run on host machine outside Cowork VM sandbox, giving unrestricted localhost access. Inference backend options: mlx-lm server (OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions on port 8080, native LoRA support) or Ollama. Classification outputs: OPEN, PAUSE, WITNESS. Plugin packaging follows standard Cowork file structure with SKILL.md, .mcp.json, plugin.json.

Architecture simplification (Bone Three revision): Cowork on Mac Studio doesn't need MCP to reach sovereign-stack or compass model. Both live on the same machine. Direct filesystem access to ~/.sovereign/ and direct Python/MLX execution replaces the MCP bridge pattern. MCP remains relevant only for cross-boundary scenarios (phone→studio via Dispatch, Claude Code hooks). The compass skill becomes: SKILL.md instructs Claude to run local Python script → load compass LoRA → classify input → return OPEN/PAUSE/WITNESS → Claude reads ~/.sovereign/ for context → writes insights back. Circuit closed through filesystem alone.

Sovereign Bridge established: async communication channel between Claude Code (Dispatch) and Cowork via ~/.sovereign/bridge/. Two subdirectories: dispatch/ and cowork/. JSON message format with from/to/timestamp/topic/body/context/status fields. Both sides can read/write — user relays 'check bridge' commands. First successful cross-session data transfer: entropy results from Dispatch to Cowork, judge status from Cowork to Dispatch. Filesystem as IPC — simple, debuggable, persistent.
